guides.prerequisites: Understand financial-statement periods, numerator and denominator scope, units, source dates, and that a ratio is evidence rather than a trade instruction.
guides.procedure: Define the reporting period and accounting scope; write the formula; substitute each fictional value with units; calculate the intermediate result; compare only like periods and stop when a required disclosure is absent.
guides.limit: Negative EPS, cyclicality, and one-time earnings can make P/E uninformative.
guides.invalidation: HOLD when period, accounting scope, numerator, denominator, units, source rights, or comparability cannot be verified. Negative EPS, cyclicality, and one-time earnings can make P/E uninformative.
guides.commonError: Trading misconception: Mixing forward price with trailing EPS without labeling the periods confuses comparison. Correct by restoring the stated formula, matching period, source scope, and units.
guides.selfCheck: Reproduce the fictional calculation, identify its denominator, correct the misconception, and state one limitation that blocks a directional conclusion.
guides.reviewExplanation: Ungraded Talia walkthrough: P/E divides a stated share price by comparable earnings per share and requires period labeling. Worked fictional evidence: Price $30 / trailing EPS $2 = 15×. Error correction: Mixing forward price with trailing EPS without labeling the periods confuses comparison. Boundary: Negative EPS, cyclicality, and one-time earnings can make P/E uninformative. No protected assessment, valuation conclusion, or trade order is created.
guides.transferQuestion: FICTIONAL independent transfer: Price $24 and EPS $1.50: compute P/E and state the earnings period needed.

sourceResearchTriage.supportedScope: SEC financial statement definitions and the limited non-GAAP free-cash-flow disclosure context help identify the indicated ratio's numerator and denominator. Lesson: Price-to-earnings ratio. Public reference addresses the underlying category; exact fictional figures are original exercises, not directly evidenced provider results.
sourceResearchTriage.limitationsAndOpenQuestions: Reported accounting ratios depend on period, numerator, denominator, recognition policy and financial statement footnotes. Negative EPS, cyclicality, and one-time earnings can make P/E uninformative. Independent formula convention, arithmetic, rights, accessibility and suitability require separate reviewers before publication.

guides.title: Price-to-sales ratio

guides.procedure: Define the reporting period and accounting scope; write the formula; substitute each fictional value with units; calculate the intermediate result; compare only like periods and stop when a required disclosure is absent.
guides.limit: Margins, dilution, and revenue quality remain unmeasured.
guides.invalidation: HOLD when period, accounting scope, numerator, denominator, units, source rights, or comparability cannot be verified. Margins, dilution, and revenue quality remain unmeasured.
guides.commonError: Trading misconception: Calling a lower P/S automatically cheaper ignores profitability and growth differences. Correct by restoring the stated formula, matching period, source scope, and units.
guides.selfCheck: Reproduce the fictional calculation, identify its denominator, correct the misconception, and state one limitation that blocks a directional conclusion.

guides.title: Simplified enterprise value
guides.concept: Simplified enterprise value adds debt to equity value and subtracts cash under a declared scope.
guides.prerequisites: Understand financial-statement periods, numerator and denominator scope, units, source dates, and that a ratio is evidence rather than a trade instruction.
guides.procedure: Define the reporting period and accounting scope; write the formula; substitute each fictional value with units; calculate the intermediate result; compare only like periods and stop when a required disclosure is absent.
guides.limit: Preferred stock, leases, minority interests, and restricted cash may be required.
guides.invalidation: HOLD when period, accounting scope, numerator, denominator, units, source rights, or comparability cannot be verified. Preferred stock, leases, minority interests, and restricted cash may be required.
guides.commonError: Trading misconception: Subtracting all reported cash without checking availability can understate EV. Correct by restoring the stated formula, matching period, source scope, and units.
guides.selfCheck: Reproduce the fictional calculation, identify its denominator, correct the misconception, and state one limitation that blocks a directional conclusion.
guides.reviewExplanation: Ungraded Talia walkthrough: Simplified enterprise value adds debt to equity value and subtracts cash under a declared scope. Worked fictional evidence: Market cap $100m + debt $30m − cash $20m = $110m. Error correction: Subtracting all reported cash without checking availability can understate EV. Boundary: Preferred stock, leases, minority interests, and restricted cash may be required. No protected assessment, valuation conclusion, or trade order is created.

guides.title: Share-count dilution rate
guides.concept: Share-count dilution compares weighted-average or period-end shares on a consistent basis.
guides.prerequisites: Understand financial-statement periods, numerator and denominator scope, units, source dates, and that a ratio is evidence rather than a trade instruction.
guides.procedure: Define the reporting period and accounting scope; write the formula; substitute each fictional value with units; calculate the intermediate result; compare only like periods and stop when a required disclosure is absent.
guides.limit: Buybacks, splits, and denominator choice affect interpretation.
guides.invalidation: HOLD when period, accounting scope, numerator, denominator, units, source rights, or comparability cannot be verified. Buybacks, splits, and denominator choice affect interpretation.
guides.commonError: Trading misconception: Calling a split-adjusted increase economic dilution without reconciliation can be wrong. Correct by restoring the stated formula, matching period, source scope, and units.
guides.selfCheck: Reproduce the fictional calculation, identify its denominator, correct the misconception, and state one limitation that blocks a directional conclusion.
guides.reviewExplanation: Ungraded Talia walkthrough: Share-count dilution compares weighted-average or period-end shares on a consistent basis. Worked fictional evidence: Shares rise from 20m to 25m: (5m/20m)×100=25%. Error correction: Calling a split-adjusted increase economic dilution without reconciliation can be wrong. Boundary: Buybacks, splits, and denominator choice affect interpretation. No protected assessment, valuation conclusion, or trade order is created.
